newsitem.title: EGYPT: Japan seeks larger private sector role in Mideast.
newsitem.headline: Japan seeks larger private sector role in Mideast.

text.p: Japan is seeking a higher private sector business profile in the Middle East and is sending an envoy to the region next week to offer support for the peace process, a Japanese official said on Wednesday.
Mitsuo Sakaba, deputy chief of mission at the Japanese embassy in Egypt, said Japan saw progress in Middle East peace efforts as essential for regional economic development.
"Everybody knows that without peace there is no hope for economic development," he told a news conference.

"They (businessmen) see much economic potential in the region," he added. "The business environment should be cleared up together with the factor of negotiations on the peace process so the huge potential of this region can be exploited."

Talks between Israel and the Palestinians are moving slowly towards implementing their peace accord. Israel wants to modify it relating to troop redeployment in Hebron for security reasons. Palestinians want to go ahead with the deal as signed.
Sakaba said Japan was sending up to 60 business delegates to the Middle East and North Africa Economic Conference to be held in Cairo on November 12 to 14.
Some Arab states have been sceptical the conference could bear any fruit before full peace was reached with Israel.
Japanese envoy Nobuo Matsunaga is to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on November 12 for talks on offering Japan's support for progress in Middle East peace.
He is also expected to meet Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on November 10, 11 or 12 but a date had not yet been fixed, Sakaba said.

"The Japanese government is ready to give any assistance for promotion of the (peace) process," he said. "We are here for the help of the parties concerned. We leave the matter to the direct negotiators. We don't seek a direct role in the process."
"Particularly the unstable political conditions can be a damaging factor to business in the region," Sakaba said.
Japan and at least six other Asian countries were trying to get a head start by convening an Egypt-Asian seminar on November 10 for business "match-making" with Egyptian counterparts.
Sakaba said Japan, traditionally an investor in Gulf Arab states, was heartened by the potential in Egypt after it signed last month an International Monetary Fund stand-by credit deal.

"I think this Egyptian reform process is a very important encouraging factor. On the negative side this peace process issue after the Netanyahu government in Israel was the negative factor...but still we want to be optimistic about the future."
